Statistical results and model provenance

Source: R/inference-results.R
inference-results.Rd

Inferential functions expose a numerical Results tibble and a Metadata list without replacing their existing plots, matrices, or reporting tables. Bare plots and tables continue to print normally; use x$Results and x$Metadata to inspect their analysis. Positional lists of plots retain their length and numeric indexing. The compatibility class stores these two fields as attributes for data frames, HTML tables, and positional lists.

Arguments

Pthresh

Significance threshold, default 0.05. An explicitly supplied value takes precedence over a legacy significance threshold argument.

PVar

P-value column used for significance decisions. Defaults to raw "PValue"; select "PValueFDR" to use Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted values. Explicit legacy p-column names remain accepted. Existing, explicitly named FDR plots and adjusted-value columns are retained.

Explicit Pthresh takes precedence over Alpha, FDRAlpha, label_q, or adjusted_significance_threshold. Pairwise star_p = "adjusted" retains its legacy adjustment method unless PVar is supplied; PVar = "PValueFDR" always selects BH. star_p = "none" suppresses legacy pairwise stars. Stars retain conventional p-value tiers within the requested cutoff.

Results

Standard columns are Outcome, Predictor, OutcomeLabel, PredictorLabel, Group, Term, Estimate, ConfLow, ConfHigh, PValue, PValueFDR, and N. Labels come from the supplied codebook or attached variable labels. Additional columns include TermLabel, EffectType, ReferenceValue, Significant, Status, and Reason, plus function-specific statistics. Unsupported quantities are typed missing values, not fabricated estimates. Diagnostic likelihood ratios retain legitimate zero and infinite estimates. Failed requested relationships remain visible with unavailable estimates and a reason. Empty requests return the same column schema with zero rows.

A legacy unadjusted correlation fallback is unavailable as an adjusted estimate: FallbackEstimate and FallbackPValue retain that alternative, while legacy matrices and plots remain accessible and the failed adjustment is recorded explicitly.

Metadata

Function, PackageVersion, Call, and Arguments identify the resolved analysis. FormulaTemplate, Models, ReferenceLevels, and Standardization describe formulas, engines, reference/comparison levels, and actual scaling values. FDRFamily describes correction membership in words. ModelCounts counts primary analyses independently of coefficient rows; auxiliary fits are recorded separately. Failed identifies unavailable requests and their reasons. Existing metadata fields are preserved.

Compatibility

Standardization and statistical methods retain their existing interpretation. Legacy reporting columns keep their original scales and names. Canonical estimates and confidence limits use the same scale, with reference value one for ratios and zero for signed differences. PlotForestFromTable(x$Results) can display supported interval estimates. Missing intervals do not imply a precise estimate. FDR calculation remains available independently of the default raw-p significance decision.

Examples

set.seed(42)
df_Example <- data.frame(outcome = rnorm(40), predictor = rnorm(40))
analysis <- MakeUnivariateRegressionTable(df_Example, "outcome", "predictor")
analysis$Results
#> # A tibble: 1 × 21
#>   Outcome OutcomeLabel OutcomeFamily EffectType Predictor PredictorLabel Term   
#>   <chr>   <chr>        <chr>         <chr>      <chr>     <chr>          <chr>  
#> 1 outcome outcome      linear        Estimate   predictor predictor      predic…
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: Level <chr>, TermLabel <chr>, N <int>, Estimate <dbl>,
#> #   StdError <dbl>, ConfLow <dbl>, ConfHigh <dbl>, PValue <dbl>,
#> #   Significant <lgl>, ReferenceValue <dbl>, PValueFDR <dbl>, Group <chr>,
#> #   Status <chr>, Reason <chr>
analysis$Metadata$Models
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   Outcome Predictor Group Status Reason Partial ModelID Formula           Engine
#>   <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>  <chr>  <lgl>   <chr>   <chr>             <chr> 
#> 1 outcome predictor NA    ok     NA     FALSE   model_1 outcome ~ predic… stats…
